title: Signing up to an online service

items.title: What you are agreeing to is clear
items.look_for: A description of the service and what counts as acceptance
items.why_it_matters: Continuing to use a service is often treated as acceptance
items.question_to_ask: What exactly am I agreeing to by signing up?

items.title: Charges and renewals are stated
items.look_for: Prices, billing cycle and whether it renews automatically
items.why_it_matters: Automatic renewal is the most common unexpected charge
items.question_to_ask: Does this renew automatically, and how do I stop it?

items.title: How to cancel is explained
items.look_for: Steps to cancel and any notice needed
items.why_it_matters: A hard cancellation route keeps you paying
items.question_to_ask: How do I cancel, and when does it take effect?

items.title: Refund terms are stated
items.look_for: When a refund is given and how long it takes
items.why_it_matters: Without a stated policy, a refund is at their discretion
items.question_to_ask: In what situations do you give a refund?

items.title: What data is collected is described
items.look_for: Categories of personal data and why they are collected
items.why_it_matters: It is what you are paying with when the service is free
items.question_to_ask: What personal data do you collect about me?

items.title: Who your data is shared with is stated
items.look_for: Third parties, advertisers or group companies named
items.why_it_matters: Sharing is usually where the real exposure is

items.title: You can get your data deleted
items.look_for: A way to delete your account and your data
items.why_it_matters: Leaving a service should not mean leaving your data behind
items.question_to_ask: How do I delete my account and my data?

items.title: How the terms can change is stated
items.look_for: Whether they may change terms and whether you are told
items.why_it_matters: Silent changes can alter what you agreed to
items.question_to_ask: Will you tell me before the terms change?

items.title: Grounds for suspension are listed
items.look_for: Reasons your account may be suspended or closed, and any appeal
items.why_it_matters: Losing access can mean losing content or money held in the account
items.question_to_ask: On what grounds can my account be closed, and can I appeal?

items.title: The limit on their liability is stated
items.look_for: A cap on what they would pay if something goes wrong
items.why_it_matters: It tells you what recovery is realistically available
items.question_to_ask: What is your liability if the service fails?

items.title: Where disputes are heard is stated
items.look_for: A named city, court or arbitration process
items.why_it_matters: A distant forum makes a small dispute impractical to pursue
items.question_to_ask: Where would a dispute be heard?

items.title: A grievance contact is given
items.look_for: A named officer, an email address or a form
items.why_it_matters: It is the first step before any external complaint

suggested_questions: How do I delete my account and my data?
Who is my data shared with?
Can they change these terms without telling me?
Where would a dispute be heard?

scenarios.title: My account is suspended without warning
The terms change while I am using the service
My data is exposed in a breach

facts_to_have_ready: The date you signed up and the plan you are on
What you were charged and when
Screenshots of the terms as they were when you signed up
Any support tickets or emails you sent
documents_to_bring: The terms and the privacy policy
Any reply you received from support
